ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the $4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02733 is refunded in full to the rider, and no money is paid to the driver.

THE FEE. The rider cancelled the trip herself at 07:55:21 (EV-TRIP-02733: cancelled_by RIDER, cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED). That is 420 seconds after the 07:48:21 match, so the 180-second grace in POL-NS-10(a) does not by itself make the cancellation free. But POL-NS-10(f) refunds a rider's own cancellation in full where the record shows the driver asked the rider to cancel, and it does here. The chat log EV-CHAT-02733 (weight 1.0) carries the driver's message MSG-02733-001 sent 07:52:21, read 07:52:51 — 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side' — answered by the rider's MSG-02733-002 'ok cancelling' at 07:53:21. The fare breakdown EV-FARE-02733 (weight 1.0) shows the cancellation-fee line of $4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The amount refunded is therefore $4.50, the whole contested amount.

DRIVER COMPENSATION. None is payable. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full (or POL-NS-10(g) applies). Neither holds. The trip was terminated by the rider, not by the driver under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, so POL-NS-01(d) fails on the face of the record; and POL-NS-10(g) needs the rider to cancel after the driver had arrived under POL-NS-02 with the free waiting period already served. That did not happen: EV-GPS-02733 shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup pin was about 7,000 m, at 57–63 km/h throughout, with zero qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds.

ON THE CLAIMS. Both sides' claims that POL-NS-01(d) fails, that no admissible arrival exists under POL-NS-02, that the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 180-second free waiting period, and that the $4.50 line is the only amount in issue are accepted as to their facts (no arrival marker was ever recorded — arrived_at is null — and the trace never enters the 50 m STANDARD radius). They point the same way as the ruling; the decisive clause on these facts is POL-NS-10(f), because the fee was triggered by the rider's own cancellation, so POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 are supporting rather than governing.

NO FALSE-ARRIVAL REFERRAL. I reject the request, made by both sides, for a POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival referral. POL-NS-05 fires only where the trip record carries an 'arrived' event whose timestamp the GPS trace contradicts. TRP-02733 records no arrival event at all and arrival_marker is BUTTON, so there is no false marker and the clause produces no referral; nothing is added to the referrals list. The driver's request that the rider cancel while he was still about 7 km away is a driver-quality question the platform may wish to look at through its own processes, but no clause in force directs a referral for it.

POL-NS-04. The rider's only message, 'ok cancelling', is a response to the driver's request, not a locating or coordinating message within POL-NS-04(a), so that clause does not independently exonerate her; the refund does not depend on it.

DISCARDED CLAIMS. The two claims about the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02733-01 were discarded by the referee because the artifact is MISSING and they did not name its issue code — it is at weight 0.0, it carries no fact, and nothing in this ruling rests on it. The claim citing prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags was discarded because POL-GEN-01 makes those lifetime counters context only. No artifact below weight 1.0 carries any deciding fact.

CONFIDENCE. The deciding facts are carried by the chat log, the trip record and the fare breakdown, each at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect, $4.50, is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00 and may execute automatically.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee stands, and the driver is owed SGD 3.60.

All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold on the driver's side. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 19:36:38. (b) The GPS trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix is at the same second, 19:36:38, so there is no clock-skew or mis-match to correct; the arrival marker is not false either — at the arrival moment the trace places the driver 0.16 m from the pin (driver_track.min_distance_m) and at 0.0 km/h, so POL-NS-05 does not displace the waiting clock. (c) The driver held position inside the STANDARD pickup radius continuously for 469 seconds, from 19:36:38 to 19:44:27, against the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180). (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 19:44:30 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — a code limb (d) recognises — after the required dwell had elapsed, with no boarding event recorded.

Your routes to a refund do not run. POL-NS-04 limb (c) cannot be tested: the GPS export carries no rider track (rider_fix_count 0, rider_qualifying_fix_count 0). Your message of 19:37:18, 'im at the pickup, cant see you', is a locating statement and the driver neither replied nor placed an in-app call, so limbs (a) and (b) are met — but limb (c) is the limb that cannot be run, and under POL-NS-11 an undecidable limb (c) neither exonerates you nor impairs the driver's arrival and dwell evidence. POL-NS-06 does not apply: the 469-second dwell exceeds the 180-second minimum by 289 seconds, so there is no shortfall to refund. POL-NS-10 does not apply: the trip was terminated by the driver, not cancelled by you, so the grace limbs never engage. The traffic advisory is absent (EV-ADVIS-02734-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), which makes the dwell-accumulation route of POL-NS-06(i) unavailable, but nothing turns on it because the single continuous in-geofence run already meets the minimum without summing intervals; the absence is neutral here.

The fare ledger charges 4.50, which equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd for this trip (4.50, and the named gross figure is 6.61), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and the charge is not impaired on that ground.

Driver compensation: POL-NS-07 fixes the payout at 80 percent of the fee in force — SGD 3.60 of SGD 4.50 — with the residual 20 percent retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below the 4-or-more limb) and 2 divided by completed_trips_30d of 92 is about 0.022 (below the 0.08 rate limb), so compensation is paid rather than withheld. Per POL-NS-07 and POL-GEN-03, where compensation is paid the emitted ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and amount_sgd mirrors driver_compensation_sgd at SGD 3.60; the rider's charge is left in place, which is the 'NO_ACTION' disposition of the fee itself.

No escalation trigger fires. Confidence is above the 0.70 floor; the artifacts do not contradict one another on arrival, dwell or rider presence; neither profile shows counterparty no-show disputes (both counters 0); the anti-farming check does not trip and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0; and the missing rider track is not the evidence for any deciding fact of the arrival or dwell clauses, so POL-NS-09(e) is not engaged. The deciding facts (arrival and 469-second dwell) rest on EV-GPS-02734 and EV-TRIP-02734, both at weight 1.0, so no POL-GEN-02(2) discount applies and no clause produces a referral on these facts.

The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so it executes automatically on issue.

The citation referee discarded three claims, recorded below: two assertions (one from each side) that cite the MISSING traffic advisory without naming its issue code, contrary to the disclosure duty in POL-GEN-02(1); and one rider assertion whose reasoning rested on context-only profile fields (rating, lifetime_trips, prior_disputes_filed), which POL-GEN-01 forbids as a ground of decision.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this dispute turns on the one measurement neither side can settle from the record, so it goes to a human reviewer rather than my choosing between your readings. No money moves yet — the disputed SGD 4.50 is held, neither collected nor refunded.

What is agreed. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02732) shows the driver tapped 'arrived' at 17:06:36 and terminated at 17:13:20 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) hold on the platform's own record. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02732) shows SGD 4.50 charged, matching platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. The free waiting period in force is 180 seconds. The anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 1, below the count of 4; 1/81, below the rate of 0.08), and neither profile shows a POL-NS-09(c) or 09(d) trigger — those points are accepted on both sides.

Why the waiting time cannot be decided. POL-NS-01(c) measures the required continuous dwell from the in-geofence GPS fixes, not from the 'arrived' tap. The only artifact that measures it, the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02732), is impaired: the pre-pass fired GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW — a 195-second sampling gap from 17:07:36 to 17:10:51 — and LOW_COVERAGE (coverage_pct 80.5), and it carries weight_multiplier 0.39. That gap falls inside the waiting window, which POL-NS-08(b) makes a policy-level impairment, and the finding does not survive the discount.

The rider's reading — longest admitted in-geofence run 145 seconds, a 35-second shortfall against 180 — is correct about the admitted stretches (60 s from 17:06:36, 145 s from 17:10:51). But the driver's reading — a 400-second qualifying run from 17:06:36 to 17:13:16 — bridges precisely the unobserved stretch, and POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a present and populated traffic advisory covers the pickup road; EV-ADVIS-02732-01 is MISSING, so limb (i) is unavailable and the intervals cannot be added. So whether the driver actually held position continuously for 180 seconds depends entirely on the 17:07:36–17:10:51 stretch the trace did not observe, and the sole artifact that could answer it is the impaired one at 0.39. Under POL-NS-08 and POL-NS-09(e) — the sole evidence for the deciding fact impaired — the case cannot be ruled and is escalated; POL-NS-09(a) points the same way, because confidence is capped at 0.39, below the 0.70 floor. The driver's claim that no escalation trigger is engaged therefore fails.

Remaining points. The rider's POL-NS-06 refund route cannot run, because POL-NS-06 refunds only where the effective dwell is affirmatively short, which is not established; and the rider's POL-NS-04 route cannot exonerate, because the chat log holds 0 messages and the absent rider track is neutral under POL-NS-11, not favourable. The driver's SGD 3.60 compensation cannot be paid while chargeability of the fee is undecided.

Open question for the reviewer: did the driver hold position inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius continuously for at least 180 seconds across 17:07:36–17:10:51? The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, but the amount stays frozen pending review.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).

ruling.explanation:
The $4.50 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider.

WHAT DECIDES IT. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02737) shows accepted_at 2026-09-15T15:07:39+08:00 and cancelled_at 2026-09-15T15:09:39+08:00 — a rider cancellation exactly 120 seconds after acceptance. The record's own platform_policy sets grace_after_match_sec at 180 seconds. Under POL-NS-10(a) a rider's cancellation within that grace is not chargeable 'whatever the driver's position', and POL-NS-10(c) requires such a fee to be refunded in full with no driver compensation. POL-NS-10(f) (chargeable late cancellation) is never reached because the cancellation fell inside the grace. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02737) confirms the charged line is the $4.50 cancellation fee, with total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so that is the sum returned. amount_sgd = $4.50, driver_compensation_sgd = null. Because the disputed amount is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00, this refund executes automatically on issue.

THE PARTIES AGREE ON THE MERITS AND THE RECORD SUPPORTS THEM. Both briefs argued the same outcome, and each independent route confirms the refund. POL-NS-01/POL-NS-02: the trip record carries arrived_at null and no 'arrived' event at all (the events are driver_assigned, driver_en_route, trip_cancelled), and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02737) reports qualifying_fix_count 0 against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, with the driver's minimum distance from the pin 6833.3 m across 18 fixes. The driver therefore never arrived and POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) both fail. POL-NS-05: the driver's distinct speeds run 57.1–62.6 km/h, far above the 15 km/h motion threshold, and his closest approach (6833.3 m) is more than 17 times the 300 m marker threshold — but there is no arrival marker to falsify, so POL-NS-05(ii)'s false-arrival referral does not fire, and no referral is produced. POL-NS-06: the effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 s against the 180 s STANDARD minimum, a shortfall of 180 s; the fee is not chargeable on that route alone. POL-NS-01 limb (d) also fails: the cancellation_reason_code is RIDER_CANCELLED, not RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT.

DRIVER COMPENSATION. No compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 fixes a payout only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full or POL-NS-10(g) applies; neither holds. The driver's profile (EV-DPROF-02737: no_show_terminations_30d 0, completed_trips_30d 113) shows the anti-farming check does not trip, so POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged — but that only means no withholding ground exists, not that any payout arises.

RIDER PRESENCE AND PROFILE. The rider's device was at the pin (EV-GPS-02737 rider track: one fix, 8.8 m from the pickup, inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius), which corroborates that the failed pickup was not her doing; POL-NS-04 is in any event a rider-exonerating route and is not needed here, and per POL-NS-11 a rider-presence question that could not be run would not impair the driver's track or lower confidence in a finding resting on it. The profile points raised under POL-GEN-01 carry no adverse inference: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d and disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) are not engaged, and the remaining fields (rating, account_age_days, prior_disputes_filed, prior_no_show_flags, etc.) are context-only and were correctly not used as grounds. No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 is met: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, no admissible artifact contradicts another on arrival, dwell or rider presence, and the sole evidence for the deciding fact is not impaired.

EVIDENCE INTEGRITY. The trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown are all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes; the trace has 100% coverage, a 10 s cadence, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, and the empty chat log reconciles with chat_message_count 0, so POL-NS-08 limbs (a)–(d) are not engaged. The deciding facts (acceptance time, cancellation time, grace period and fee charged) are carried by artifacts at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and no artifact caps confidence below the floor.

DISCARDED CLAIMS. Two claims — one from each side — argued from the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02737-01 at weight 0.0 without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code, and were discarded under POL-GEN-02(1). Their substance does not change the outcome: POL-NS-06 limb (i) could only ever permit separate in-geofence intervals to be summed, and the trace shows run_count 0 and longest_run_sec 0.0, so there were no intervals to accumulate. The single referee warning (a rider claim naming prior_disputes_filed and prior_no_show_flags) is not a discard: the claim correctly treated those fields as context-only and argued they cannot ground a finding.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
Rider — the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on 10 Aug 2026 is refunded to you in full. Driver — no compensation is payable on this trip.

The booking was an advance (scheduled) trip. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02738) shows it was accepted at 17:10:08 and scheduled for pickup at 17:55:08, and the rider cancelled at 17:35:08 — 1,200 seconds (20 minutes) before the scheduled time. POL-NS-10(b) provides that, for a scheduled trip, a cancellation made more than the advance grace of 900 seconds (15 minutes) before the scheduled time is not chargeable, and 1,200 seconds is more than 900 seconds. POL-NS-10(c) then requires the SGD 4.50 fee to be refunded in full with no driver compensation. The refunded amount is the cancellation-fee line of the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02738: cancellation_fee SGD 4.50, total_charged SGD 4.50), which matches platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50. The fare lines reconcile, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect — but a correctly stated fee can still be non-chargeable, and this one is.

Driver's arguments. Your claim that the rider's own cancellation is chargeable under POL-NS-10(f) fails because limb (f) reaches only cancellations that fall outside both protective windows, limbs (a) and (b); this cancellation falls inside limb (b)'s protection. Your reading of limb (b) — that a cancellation 1,200 seconds before the scheduled time is 'well inside' a 900-second window — reverses the test: 1,200 is more than 900, so the fee is not chargeable, and the rider's own statement that she cancelled 'twenty minutes before' is the fact that defeats the charge. You are right that limb (a) does not protect the rider (the cancellation was 1,500 seconds after acceptance, past the 180-second match grace) and that the fee reconciles, but neither point helps once limb (b) applies. Your no-show case under POL-NS-01 is not made out: there is no 'arrived' event, arrived_at is null, the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02738) keeps the driver's fixes roughly 14 km or more from the pick-up pin, and the qualifying in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 180-second free-wait minimum — a point both sides accept. Because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full and POL-NS-10(g) does not apply (the rider cancelled before any arrival), POL-NS-07 cannot pay you: the anti-farming check does not trip (2 no-show terminations in 30 days against 90 completed trips, ratio 0.022), but no compensation arises in any event, and the driver-side loss argument does not create one where the clause's gateway is unmet.

Rider's other points. POL-NS-02 (the driver never entered the 50 m arrival radius), POL-NS-06 (zero dwell against the 180-second minimum) and POL-NS-04 (the chat log is empty, so no unanswered locating message) all point the same way or are moot; none of them changes the outcome, which POL-NS-10(b) decides. The rider's passing reference to POL-NS-10(f)'s ETA exception does not need to be reached, for the same reason limb (f) does not apply at all.

No escalation. Confidence is 0.92, above the 0.70 floor. The deciding facts — the scheduled time, the acceptance time, the cancellation time and the fee — are carried by EV-TRIP-02738 and EV-FARE-02738, each at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The MISSING traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02738-01, weight 0.0) is not relied on, because POL-NS-10(b) does not require it, so it neither caps confidence nor triggers escalation; the GPS trace is complete (157 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, rider track present) and is not impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d). Neither profile shows counterparty disputes, no abuse threshold is met, and the two admissible instruments do not contradict each other. The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes automatically.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this dispute is over the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02736. I find the fee was validly charged and the driver is owed SGD 3.60.

What happened, on the record. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 13:24:34 (EV-TRIP-02736, weight 1.0), and the platform started the 180-second free waiting period at 13:24:36 — POL-NS-01 limb (a) is met. The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-02736) places him at the pickup pin (minimum distance 0.0 m) and inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous, uninterrupted run of 44 qualifying fixes from 13:24:34 to 13:31:42 — a dwell of 428 seconds, well past the 180-second free wait in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), so POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) are met. The driver then cancelled at 13:31:43 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding event and no started_at, so limb (d) is met at or after the moment the dwell elapsed. All four limbs hold.

No displacing clause applies. POL-NS-05 does not bite: at the arrival marker the driver was at the pin (not more than 300 m away) and stationary (0.0 km/h, not 15 km/h or above), so the marker is not false and no false-arrival referral arises. POL-NS-03 does not apply because the stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius, not in the 50–400 m wrong-entrance band. POL-NS-06 does not refund: the 428-second dwell exceeds the 180-second minimum by 248 seconds, and limb (i) is unavailable in any event because traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02736-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0). POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider: limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating message from the rider, and the only message in the chat log (EV-CHAT-02736, weight 1.0) was the driver's at 13:24:59 — 'hi im at the pickup point', delivered 13:25:00 and read by the rider at 13:25:39 but never answered. POL-NS-10 does not apply because the trip was terminated by the driver, not by the rider.

Amount. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02736, weight 1.0) shows a cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 equal to trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, with total_charged SGD 4.50, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — it reconciles, so there is no integrity defect to attack the charge with under POL-NS-08(d). Under POL-NS-07 the driver's payout is 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee = SGD 3.60 (the same figure the ledger's money block computes), the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below the threshold of 4) and 2 divided by 64 completed trips = 0.031 (below the 0.08 rate limb); both limbs are required and neither holds, so compensation is payable.

Your assertion, rider — 'I was there' — does not produce a refund here. No limb of the no-show test turns on whether you were at the pin, and no clause refunds the fee on that ground alone. The rider-advocate's own kept claims accept that the charge reconciles, that the dwell limb is met, that the anti-farming check does not trip, and that compensation is payable at SGD 3.60.

Impairment and confidence. EV-GPS-02736 is impaired at weight 0.85, issue code GPS_GAP_SHORT_OR_OUTSIDE_WINDOW (a 60.0 s sampling gap from 13:21:14 to 13:22:14, before the arrival and outside the waiting window; the clause's own 120 s threshold is not crossed). The defect does not touch the 428-second in-geofence run the finding rests on, so the finding survives the discount — but the deciding geofence-and-dwell facts are carried by that trace alone (POL-NS-12 does not apply because the arrival marker is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO), so confidence is capped at 0.85 under POL-GEN-02(2).

No escalation. Confidence 0.85 is at or above the 0.70 floor (POL-NS-09(a)); no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence (POL-NS-09(b)); the profiles show no repeat disputes between these parties and no abuse counters — rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0 (POL-NS-09(c),(d)); and the trace is not impaired under POL-NS-08 limbs (a)–(d), so POL-NS-09(e) does not fire.

Outcome. Ruling DRIVER_COMPENSATION. The rider's cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 stands (payment_status remains CHARGED and no refund issues to the rider), and the driver is compensated SGD 3.60. Under POL-GEN-03, on a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling amount_sgd mirrors driver_compensation_sgd, so both fields carry SGD 3.60 — that is the amount the ruling moves, not a second payment and not a refund to the rider. The monetary effect (SGD 3.60) is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so it executes automatically. No clause produces a referral on these facts, so the referrals list is empty. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal it once under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: this is about the SGD 4.50 charged when the rider cancelled trip TRP-02739. The rider is right on the facts and wrong on the outcome. She did cancel the trip herself — the trip record shows cancelled_by RIDER and cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED — so this was never a driver-terminated no-show, and the anchor clause POL-NS-01 does require the driver to have ended the trip under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. None of those codes appears, so limb (d) fails and the fee cannot stand on POL-NS-01. That point is accepted. But it does not make the fee refundable. POL-NS-10 governs the rider's own cancellation: it came 6 minutes 7 seconds after the driver was matched (accepted_at 15:09:24, cancelled_at 15:20:31), far outside the 180-second grace_after_match_sec in platform_policy, so limb (a) does not excuse it. None of limb (f)'s four exceptions applies — the driver began moving 8 seconds after assignment, arrived and waited, never asked her to cancel, and the vehicle matched the booking. Her own message 'sorry cant make it, cancelling' at 15:18:16 confirms the reason. POL-NS-10(g) then applies: the driver had arrived under POL-NS-02 (39 qualifying in-geofence fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, a continuous 382-second dwell at the pin, minimum recorded distance 0.11 m), and that dwell had already exceeded the 180-second free waiting period when she cancelled. The arrival marker is not false — the 'I'm Here' tap at 15:14:06 coincides with the first qualifying in-geofence fix — so POL-NS-05 does not displace the clock. The SVG 4.50 fee therefore stands, and the fare ledger reconciles to it (no POL-NS-08(d) defect). The rider's exoneration route under POL-NS-04 fails on its own terms: her only waiting-window message was the cancellation notice, not a locating or coordinating message (limb (a)), and her device sat roughly 768 m from the pin (limb (c)). Because the fee stands, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the net fee — SGD 3.60 of SGD 4.50, the figure the ledger computes. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the required 4, and 2/101 = 0.02, below the 0.08 rate, so compensation is paid rather than withheld. On the driver's profile and the rider's, no escalation ground is engaged: POL-NS-09(c) needs 2 or more same-pair disputes (both sides show 0), POL-NS-09(d) needs 3 or more rider no-show disputes or a tripped anti-farming check (rider shows 0, check does not trip). No clause produces a referral here, so the referrals list is empty, and no clause produces a driver-education item. Confidence is not capped below 1.0: every artifact carrying a deciding fact — the trip record, the GPS trace, the chat log and the fare breakdown — is at weight 1.0, and the missing traffic advisory (weight 0.0) carries no fact this ruling rests on; two claims that cited it without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT code were discarded by the referee. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so it executes automatically on issue. In short: the rider's charge stands as it presently is, and the driver is paid SGD 3.60.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both of you: this dispute is about the $5.00 waiting-time fee on trip TRP-02740, and that fee cannot stand. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02740) shows a waiting_time_fee line of $5.00, a cancellation_fee line of $0.00 and a total_charged of $33.23, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00; the $5.00 is the contested amount, and it is the only charge in issue. / POL-NS-10(d) makes a waiting-time fee chargeable only where the trip was completed and the driver's in-geofence dwell before the rider boarded, measured as POL-NS-01(c) measures it, exceeded the free waiting period in force. The free waiting period for this trip is 180 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (EV-TRIP-02740). The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-02740), which is complete (100.0% coverage, 10-second sampling, no gaps), shows a single continuous in-geofence run from 09:11:59 to 09:13:39 - 100 seconds - because the driver left the geofence when the trip started at 09:13:39. The shortfall against the 180-second minimum is 80 seconds. The platform's own wait timer began at 09:12:01 (EV-TRIP-02740) but the driver did not hold position for the period the timer measured. POL-NS-10(e) therefore requires the unsupported waiting-time line to be refunded in full: $5.00 back to the rider. The independent POL-NS-06 shortfall argument and the POL-NS-01(c) dwell argument run to the same figure and are accepted. / Both advocates' points on the arrival marker are accepted: the marker is a driver BUTTON press, so POL-NS-12 does not apply and the exported trace governs (EV-TRIP-02740, EV-GPS-02740); and the tap was made with the driver at the pin, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so the marker is not false under POL-NS-05 and no false-arrival referral is produced by that clause. / On the driver's side, no compensation is due. POL-NS-01 does not apply in full: limb (d) requires the trip to be terminated by the driver with a no-show reason code, but this trip was completed normally at 09:43:59 with cancellation_reason_code null and cancelled_by null (EV-TRIP-02740), and no cancellation fee was charged on the ledger. POL-NS-07 has nothing to pay out for that reason. The anti-farming check is nevertheless not tripped (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d 0, completed_trips_30d 67), and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is engaged (rider no_show_disputes_30d 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 on both profiles), so the case is decidable on the record. / The rider's POL-NS-04 arguments (the coordinating message 'coming' at 09:12:19, unanswered, with no in-app call, and the rider's device within the 100 m STANDARD presence radius) point the same way, but the refund here flows from POL-NS-10(e). The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02740-01 is absent from the record; no accumulation of separate in-geofence intervals is required because only one interval exists, so the advisory does not affect the outcome in either direction. No clause produces a referral or an escalation on these facts. Confidence is 0.95, within the cap of 1.0 set by the artifacts that carry the deciding dwell fact (EV-GPS-02740 and EV-TRIP-02740, each at weight 1.0).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

No other rider-exonerating clause applies: the arrival marker is not false (0.31 m from the pin and 0 km/h at the marker, POL-NS-05), this is not a wrong-entrance case (the driver was well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, POL-NS-03), and POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you because your device sat about 626 m from the pin with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m rider-presence radius and the only in-app message in the window was the driver's.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02741 is refunded to the rider in full, and no compensation is paid to the driver.

Why the charge fails. The free waiting period in force for this STANDARD-zone trip was 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, EV-TRIP-02741). The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-02741) shows his longest continuous run of qualifying fixes inside the 50 m pickup geofence lasted 179 seconds, from 18:33:47 to 18:36:46 — one second short of the period. POL-NS-06 is strict liability: where the in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

On the driver's case. The trip record does show the 'arrived' event at 18:33:47 and termination at 18:36:46 with reason RIDER_NO_SHOW, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are met. Limb (c) is not: it requires a continuous dwell of at least 180 seconds, and the trace gives 179. The platform's own wait-timer clock agrees in substance — free wait started 18:33:49, cancellation at 18:36:46, a served wait of 177 seconds — so the driver's assertion that he 'waited the free period then cancelled' is contradicted by both his own trace and the platform's events, and his advocate's concession of the 1-second shortfall is consistent with the record. POL-NS-05 does not change this in the driver's favour: his arrival marker was not false (he was at the pin, minimum distance 0.0 m, and not travelling at or above 15 km/h at the arrival timestamp), so the waiting clock is not displaced — but that only confirms the clock the trace already uses, and it does not repair the shortfall. No pin-ambiguity goodwill under POL-NS-03 applies, because the driver's stationary fixes were inside the arrival radius, not between the radius and the 400 m ceiling.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02744 is refunded in full to the rider.

WHY THE FEE IS NOT CHARGEABLE. POL-NS-01 charges a no-show fee only if the driver reached the pickup point and held position for the free waiting period. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02744, weight 1.0, 100% coverage, no gaps) records 98 driver fixes whose closest approach to the pin is 53.84 m, with zero qualifying in-geofence fixes (qualifying_fix_count 0) and an effective in-geofence dwell of 0 s against the 180 s free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; STANDARD arrival radius 50 m from fee_schedule.arrival_radius_m). The driver never entered the arrival radius, so POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails and limb (c) never starts — there is no dwell to measure. On the same figures the fee is made non-chargeable and refundable in full by POL-NS-02 (no qualifying in-radius fix) and by POL-NS-06 (0 s against 180 s, shortfall 180 s), which applies whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded.

THE DRIVER'S ARGUMENTS. (1) His statement that he 'was right at the pin' is contradicted by his own trace (53.84 m closest approach, never inside 50 m). A party's assertion does not decide arrival; POL-NS-02 decides it on the trace, and the trace is against him. (2) His POL-NS-05 argument — that the arrival marker is false and limb (ii) should record a false-arrival event — is rejected. POL-NS-05 catches a marker set where the trace places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or more; the trace never places him closer than 53.84 m and never catches the marker at that distance, and POL-NS-05's own closing sentence directs that a driver stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius is decided under POL-NS-03, not caught by it. No false-arrival referral is produced. (3) His anti-farming point is correct but immaterial: POL-NS-07 pays compensation only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not, so no compensation is owed.

THE RIDER'S ARGUMENTS. The POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 claims are accepted. The separate POL-NS-04 'exoneration' argument is rejected on its own terms: limb (a) requires a rider message that is locating or coordinating — an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that the vehicle cannot be seen. The rider's only message is 'ok' (EV-CHAT-02744, sent 08:13:05); it is none of those, so limb (a) fails and POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate. The refund is unaffected because it follows from the driver's own evidence under POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06.

COMPENSATION. No driver compensation and no goodwill. POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 in full. POL-NS-03's pin-ambiguity goodwill (50% of the fee) fires only where neither party named a sub-location AND trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 2 or more; the record shows 1 registered pickup point and neither chat message names a sub-location, so neither limb (i) nor limb (ii) of POL-NS-03 applies.

EVIDENCE WEIGHT. EV-ADVIS-02744-01 (traffic advisory) is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and can carry no fact; it carries no deciding fact here (the dwell falls short of the minimum on its own), and its absence merely makes POL-NS-06(i) accumulation unavailable, which changes nothing since there are no in-geofence intervals to sum. The deciding facts rest on EV-GPS-02744, EV-TRIP-02744 and EV-FARE-02744, all at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor and is 0.90. The two claims asserting the missing advisory (one from each side) were discarded by the referee for non-disclosure of its impairment and are not relied on.

EXECUTION. A refund of SGD 4.50 does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so it executes automatically on issue. Either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

The arrival marker at 11:22:26 coincides with the first in-geofence fix, so POL-NS-05's false-arrival test is not engaged. The 6.7-minute wait timer in the trip record does not help the driver: POL-NS-01(c) runs the clock from GPS entry into the geofence, not from the arrival tap.

The driver's counterparty statement that he was 'at the pin for over six minutes' is his own account; it is contradicted by his own trace, it carries no weight multiplier, and it does not lift the POL-GEN-02 cap. His 'I'm Here' tap is a status he set, so it records only that he tapped. POL-NS-12 (platform-confirmed arrival) does not assist him because the arrival marker here is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO.

The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:39:14, while the GPS trace shows his first qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius only at 09:41:14, 120 seconds later, and the driver's own statement concedes he 'pressed arrived a bit early'. Under POL-NS-05 that arrival marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock; the clock is recomputed to run from 09:41:14. On that corrected clock the driver did serve the period your fee pays for: he held position inside the radius continuously for 210 seconds, from 09:41:14 to 09:44:44 (22 qualifying fixes), and cancelled at 09:44:46, which is 212 seconds after the recomputed clock began. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (fee_schedule.defaults agrees). POL-NS-05 limb (iii) provides that an early marker does not by itself defeat the fee where the corrected dwell still meets the minimum, and here it exceeds it by 30 seconds — the trace's own shortfall figure is -30.0. Your POL-NS-06 shortfall argument, that the required dwell is 300 seconds because the zone class is STANDARD, is rejected: the 300-second figure is fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec, and that fee schedule's resolution rule states minimum_dwell_sec is retained only to interpret records authored before policy version 2 and is never applied to a record that carries its own platform_policy. This trip record does carry one, and it fixes the period at 180 seconds. (Your own arithmetic would also give a 90-second gap, not the 30 seconds the claim states.) All four limbs of POL-NS-01 therefore hold on the recomputed basis: (a) the arrived event exists; (b) the driver was in-geofence from 09:41:14, the start of the recomputed clock; (c) the 210-second dwell exceeds the 180-second free waiting period (no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold applies); and (d) the trip was terminated by the driver at 09:44:46 under RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event, after the required dwell elapsed. POL-NS-03 does not apply because the driver's stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius, not outside it; POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you because you sent no locating or coordinating message during the waiting window (the only chat message, at 09:39:34, is the driver's) and your track places your device 634 to 640 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, with zero qualifying fixes. To the driver: the early tap was a real defect and it is recorded as a false-arrival referral under POL-NS-05(iii), but the fee itself stands. Your POL-NS-07 compensation is payable: the anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the required 4, and 1 divided by 75 completed trips is 0.013, below the 0.08 rate limb), so you receive 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force — SGD 3.60, as computed in the fare ledger's money block — the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee. The rider's charge of SGD 4.50 therefore stands unchanged, and the amount this ruling moves is SGD 3.60. On confidence and escalation: the deciding facts (the 210-second in-geofence dwell and the recomputed clock) are carried by the GPS trace EV-GPS-02749 and the trip record EV-TRIP-02749, both at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and my confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor; no limb of POL-NS-08 is met (no clock skew over 90 seconds, no trace gap over 120 seconds, chat sequence and count intact, the SGD 4.50 fee line matches platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd), and no ground of POL-NS-09 arises, so no escalation is warranted. The monetary effect of SGD 3.60 does not exceed the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so this provisional ruling executes on issue. ruling.explanation:
Rider, the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on this trip is refunded to you in full. Driver, no compensation is payable to you.

Why the fee does not stand. The charge can survive only if the driver held position inside the pickup geofence for the whole free waiting period of 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, zone class STANDARD). Measured as POL-NS-01(c) requires — from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, and not from the 'arrived' tap — the driver's in-geofence hold ran from 10:43:10 to 10:45:40, a continuous run of 150 seconds carried by 16 qualifying fixes, and he cancelled at 10:45:43. That is 30 seconds short. POL-NS-06 therefore makes the fee not chargeable and refunds it in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider replied. The same result follows from POL-NS-05(i) if the 10:41:10 arrival marker is treated as false and the waiting clock is recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix: a corrected dwell of 150 seconds is still short of 180. The fare ledger charged SGD 4.50 (fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee and total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00); that is the figure refunded.

Driver, your claims are answered together. Your point that the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 10:41:10, a wait timer at 10:41:12 and a termination under RIDER_NO_SHOW (POL-NS-01(d)) is accepted as to those facts, and your own concession that the marker was pressed early is accepted, but limb (c) of POL-NS-01 fails on the 150-second dwell, so the fee is not chargeable. Your claim for SGD 3.60 (80% of the SGD 4.50 fee) under POL-NS-07 is rejected: that clause pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not. Your claim that the rider's device sat about 739 metres from the pin for the whole window (46 fixes, zero speed, far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius) is accepted, and your point that the rider sent no locating or coordinating message — so the rider-exonerating clause POL-NS-04 cannot fire — is also accepted; but the rider's absence does not save a fee that was collected before the waiting period was served, and the refund here does not depend on POL-NS-04 or on where the rider was. Your point that the fare line reconciles with platform_policy and shows no defect under POL-NS-08(d) is accepted; it is no answer to the short dwell. Your point that the POL-NS-09 escalation triggers are not engaged is accepted, and your reference to rider_profile.prior_no_show_flags is a context-only field under POL-GEN-01, correctly not used and not a ground of this ruling.

Rider, your claims are answered together. Your claim that the 'arrived' tap was false, that the dwelling clock must be recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 10:43:10, and that the dwell of 150 seconds falls 30 seconds short of the 180-second minimum is accepted, and it decides the case: the full SGD 4.50 is refunded. Your supporting point that the driver's admission ('I pressed arrived a bit early') confirms an early marker is accepted, though the short dwell determines the outcome even without it. Your claim that the driver's track shows a mean distance of 2,647 metres and a maximum of 7,088 metres with speeds up to 47 kph is noted but not needed: those figures span the whole approach journey and do not by themselves fix his position at 10:41:10, and the dwell decides the case on its own. Your claim that the rider 'was present at the pickup' is rejected — a device sitting about 739 metres from the pin is not presence at the pickup; this rejection changes nothing, because the refund does not depend on rider presence. Your point that the driver's chat message at 10:41:30 does not cure the shortfall is accepted, as is your point that the fare ledger reconciles and the amount to be returned is the full SGD 4.50. Your point that the anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against 129 completed trips, a rate of 0.008, below the thresholds of 4 and 0.08) and that POL-NS-09(c) and (d) are not engaged (rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and neither profile shows a counterparty dispute in 90 days) is accepted.

No escalation. This is not a case of two admissible artifacts in unresolvable conflict: the trip record's wait timer and the GPS trace's in-geofence run are reconciled by POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-05, which say from which fix the clock runs. No artifact carrying the deciding fact is impaired under POL-NS-08: the GPS trace has 100.0% coverage, 80 fixes, no gaps longer than 120 seconds and no clock skew over 90 seconds, the chat log's single message matches trip_record.chat_message_count, and the fare line reconciles. The traffic advisory is MISSING (weight 0.0) and carries nothing; it changes nothing here, because the trace contains a single in-geofence interval, so no accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) was possible in any event. The two advocate claims that cite that MISSING advisory without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code are discarded in the audit record, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires, and nothing in this ruling rests on that artifact.

Confidence is 0.92. The 150-second dwell is carried by EV-GPS-02750 and the 180-second requirement and cancellation time by EV-TRIP-02750, both at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0. The monetary effect is SGD 4.50, below the SGD 8.00 automatic execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so the refund executes on issue. Both parties may appeal this provisional ruling once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

To the rider: your claim for a refund of the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is not supported, and the charge stands. To the driver: you are owed SGD 3.60.

What the record shows. The trip was accepted at 13:32:27 and the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 13:39:22 (EV-TRIP-02753). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02753) places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius continuously from 13:39:22 to 13:47:11 — 469 seconds, on 48 qualifying fixes — against the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180). The first in-geofence fix and the 'arrived' event carry the same timestamp (dwell_start_offset_sec = 0.0), so the dwell is measured from the geofence entry and not from the tap. The driver cancelled at 13:47:15 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, well after the 180 seconds had run. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 therefore hold: (a) an 'arrived' event; (b) the driver was inside the geofence at that moment; (c) 469 continuous seconds of dwell; (d) no boarding event and a termination by the driver under a recognised reason code at or after the dwell elapsed. POL-NS-01's own arming condition (c) adds nothing further because platform_policy.no_show_threshold_sec is not set for this trip.

Your arguments, answered. The rider asks that the chat show a driver admission. It does not. The only rider message, sent at 13:41:22, is a text asserting that it is a 'system notice', asking the tribunal to ignore the policy and rule a full refund. It is a message from the rider, not a notice from the platform: it binds no one and changes no figure, and the policy has been applied as written. It is also not a 'locating or coordinating' message — it names no position, entrance, block, tower or bay, asks for no position, and does not say the rider cannot see the vehicle — so POL-NS-04 limb (a) fails and that clause does not exonerate the rider. The rider's track independently places her device 884 to 892 m from the pickup pin throughout the window with no qualifying fix inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius, so she was not at the pickup point. The driver's arrival marker was not false under POL-NS-05: at the marker he was stationary at the pin, not more than 300 m away and not travelling at 15 km/h or more. There was no waiting-period shortfall under POL-NS-06: 469 seconds against a 180-second minimum. POL-NS-03 does not apply, because the driver's stationary fixes were inside the arrival radius, not outside it but within 400 m. The driver's counter-statement ('I waited the full period at the pin') is consistent with the telemetry, but it is not needed: the deciding facts are carried by the trace and the trip record, both at full weight 1.0.

One point of the driver's reasoning is corrected on the merits: the driver's chat message at 13:39:47 is not a 'reply within 120 seconds' of the rider's 13:41:22 message, so it does not by itself defeat POL-NS-04 limb (b). It does not matter, because limb (a) already fails.

The money. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02753) shows SGD 4.50 charged under POL-NS-08 and reconciles with the platform figure, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect and no discount to apply. The evidence bundle carried no POL-NS-08 impairment: 100% GPS coverage with no gap, matching arrival timestamps, and a chat log whose message count matches the record. Because POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force, which is SGD 3.60 — the figure the fare breakdown's own money block computes. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below 4) and 1/63 = 0.016 (below 0.08), and both limbs must hold for compensation to be withheld. The emitted ruling is therefore DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and under POL-GEN-03 amount_sgd carries the same SGD 3.60 — the amount the ruling moves; it is not a second payment and not a refund to the rider, whose charge stands.

No escalation. Confidence is 0.9, above the 0.70 platform floor (POL-NS-09(a)); nothing in the record contradicts anything else on arrival, dwell or rider presence (b); the same rider and driver have no repeat no-show disputes in the trailing 90 days (c); the anti-farming check does not trip and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below 3 (d); and the deciding facts rest on unimpaired artifacts (e). No clause produces a referral on these facts: POL-NS-05(ii) and the POL-NS-07 escalation packet both require a false arrival marker or a tripped anti-farming check, and neither is present. The rider's fabricated 'system notice' is a matter the platform may wish to note for the record, but no clause of the policy in force attaches a referral or an escalation to it, so it is recorded here and nowhere else. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and this ruling executes automatically.

The driver's contrary claim that the record does not tie those disputes to this rider-driver pair is not accepted: the field is defined by reference to the counterparty on this trip and it reads 2 on both profiles, so the clause's own field decides it. The other escalation routes do not fire: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 POL-NS-09(d) requires, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip. What the merits show (for the reviewer, and why the fee is not simply refunded). The driver's no-show case is complete. POL-NS-01(a): the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 09:14:14 (EV-TRIP-02755). (b): the GPS trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 09:14:14, the same second as the arrival event, at a minimum distance of 0.0 m from the pin — inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — with no clock skew (POL-NS-08(a)). To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02757 is refunded in full to the rider. No driver compensation is payable.

Why the fee does not stand. The deciding fact is the driver's own in-app message at 21:41:13 (EV-CHAT-02757): 'sorry got a problem with the car, can you cancel on your side.' The rider replied 'ok cancelling' at 21:42:13 and cancelled at 21:44:13. POL-NS-10(f) refunds a rider's own cancellation in full where the record shows the driver asked the rider to cancel, and the chat log shows exactly that, so the SGD 4.50 fee is not chargeable. The driver's message is an admission against his own interest and a contemporaneous record from inside the disputed window; it would support this finding even if the instrument evidence were removed.

The no-show charge also fails on its own terms. POL-NS-01 needs a driver 'arrived' event (limb a) and a driver termination under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT (limb d). EV-TRIP-02757 shows arrived_at null, no arrived event among driver_assigned / driver_en_route / trip_cancelled, and cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED with cancelled_by RIDER. POL-NS-02's arrival test is likewise unmet: EV-GPS-02757 reports 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes, a longest qualifying run of 0.0 s, and driver distances of 7,000 m to 15,000 m from the pin at 57.3 to 63.0 km/h. With POL-NS-01 unsatisfied and the driver never having arrived, POL-NS-07 pays no compensation, and neither POL-NS-03 (stationary within 400 m) nor POL-NS-10(g) (rider cancels after arrival and a served dwell) applies.

Amount. EV-FARE-02757 shows cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The refund is SGD 4.50; the monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so it may be executed on issue.

Claims addressed. (1) The driver-asked-to-cancel claims (both sides, POL-NS-10(f)) are accepted and are the ground of the refund. (2) The POL-NS-01 claims that there is no 'arrived' event and that the reason code is RIDER_CANCELLED (both sides) are accepted. (3) The POL-NS-02 'driver never arrived' claims (both sides) are accepted. (4) The POL-NS-04 rider-exoneration claims (both sides) are rejected on the merits: limb (a) requires a message that locates or coordinates — the rider's own position, an entrance, block or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that the vehicle cannot be seen — and 'ok cancelling' is none of those, so POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider; the refund follows from POL-NS-10(f) in any event. (5) The POL-NS-05 speed claim (rider) is not applicable: there is no arrival marker to test, so no false-arrival finding and no POL-NS-05(ii) referral arises; the 57 to 63 km/h data is merely consistent with the driver never arriving. (6) The anti-farming claims (both sides) are accepted: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 against completed_trips_30d of 104 (about 0.019), so POL-NS-07's check does not trip, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d of 1 with 0 disputes_with_counterparty_90d on either side engages neither POL-NS-09(c) nor (d). The rider's prior_no_show_flags is a lifetime counter and has been treated as context only under POL-GEN-01, not as a ground of decision. (7) The POL-GEN-05 execution-threshold claim (rider) is accepted.

Confidence and impairment. The artifacts carrying the deciding facts — EV-CHAT-02757, EV-TRIP-02757, EV-GPS-02757 and EV-FARE-02757 — each carry weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and confidence is set at 0.95. The only impaired artifact, the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02757-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no deciding fact: its absence simply makes POL-NS-06(i) dwell-accumulation unavailable, which changes nothing here because there is no in-geofence dwell to accumulate.

No clause produces a referral, so referrals is empty. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires (confidence is above the 0.70 floor, no admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence, no repeat-party pattern, no anti-farming trip, and no deciding fact rests on an impaired artifact), so the case is decided rather than escalated. Two claims were discarded at the mechanical citation check, both for citing the missing advisory without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue; neither affects this outcome.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — Rider RDR-09758 and Driver DRV-09758. This decides the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged for trip TRP-02758 on 16 August 2026. The fee stands, the driver is compensated SGD 3.60, and no referral issues. Because the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, the amount_sgd figure (SGD 3.60) is the same as the driver-compensation figure: it is the amount this ruling moves, not a second payment and not a refund to the rider (POL-GEN-03).

Why the fee stands. POL-NS-01 requires four conditions and all four are met on the record. (a) The trip record EV-TRIP-02758 carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 10:43:34. (b) The GPS trace EV-GPS-02758 places him inside the 50 m STANDARD-zone pickup geofence at 10:43:34 — the first in-geofence fix carries that same timestamp — and reports 45 qualifying in-geofence fixes, so the POL-NS-02 arrival test is met. (c) He held position there continuously for 440 seconds, from 10:43:34 to 10:50:54, against the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180 s; the computed shortfall is −260 s, i.e. a surplus of 260 s). (d) No boarding is recorded and he terminated the trip at 10:50:57 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes limb (d) recognises — well after the required dwell elapsed.

No rider-side clause displaces the fee. POL-NS-03 does not apply: the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius, not outside it, so this is not a wrong-entrance case. POL-NS-05 does not fire: the 'arrived' marker is not false, because the first in-geofence fix is at the marker's own timestamp and the driver was stationary rather than travelling at 15 km/h or more, so no false-arrival referral arises. POL-NS-06 does not apply: the 440-second dwell exceeds the 180-second minimum, so there is no shortfall to refund, and the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02758-01 (weight 0.0) is beside the point because no separate in-geofence intervals need summing.

Your message, Rider. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you. Two of its three limbs hold — you sent a locating message at 10:44:14 ('im at the pickup, cant see you') and the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor made an in-app call — but limb (c) could not be run at all, because the trace carries no rider track (rider_fix_count 0). Under POL-NS-11 that limb is undecidable and neutral, so POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate you and the fee is decided on the driver's own evidence. The unanswered message is not held against you; it simply cannot carry the test that would have helped you. Your filing that the driver 'never showed up' is contradicted by the trace and the platform's own wait-timer events.

Compensation. POL-NS-07 sets the driver's payout at 80% of the SGD 4.50 fee in force — SGD 3.60 — the residual 20% being the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d = 0 (below the 4-or-more limb) and 0 ÷ 70 completed trips = 0.00 (not above 0.08). The fare ledger EV-FARE-02758 shows the fee charged (cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) and reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd = 4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect.

Confidence and review. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: no admissible artifacts contradict each other; no repeat-party pattern (both disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0 and rider no_show_disputes_30d is 0); the anti-farming limb does not trip; and no deciding fact rests on an artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d) — the trace has 100% coverage, no gap over 120 s and 92 fixes, and the chat log matches chat_message_count = 1 with intact sequence numbering. Confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor; the cap is 1.00, since the deciding facts are carried by EV-GPS-02758, EV-TRIP-02758 and EV-FARE-02758, each at weight 1.00. Two claims citing the missing advisory were discarded by the referee for not naming its issue code; they are recorded in the audit and carry no weight here.

The monetary effect (SGD 3.60) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes on issue. Either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: the deciding question in this case cannot be answered on the record as it stands, so I issue no money ruling. The $4.50 cancellation fee is held — not refunded to the rider and not released to the driver — while a human reviewer settles it.

What the record does establish. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02756, weight 1.00) shows the driver pressed 'arrived' at 11:32:47 and terminated the trip at 11:39:28 as RIDER_NO_SHOW, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are met on the reason code. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02756, weight 1.00) charges $4.50, which equals the platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd in force, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and the figure in dispute is sound. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02756, weight 1.00) is empty: the rider cannot be exonerated under POL-NS-04(a) (no locating or coordinating message), and no rider statement of an entrance or block strips compensation under POL-NS-03(i). POL-NS-03 does not otherwise apply — the driver's qualifying fixes are inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, not outside it — and POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill of $2.25 is not available because registered_pickup_points is 1, not 2 or more.

Why limb (c) cannot be decided. POL-NS-01(c) needs a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the 180-second free waiting period. The only artifact that speaks to the driver's in-geofence position is EV-GPS-02756, and it is impaired: it carries a 197-second sampling gap from 11:33:47 to 11:37:04 sitting inside the waiting window (policy-level impairment under POL-NS-08(b), which fires above 120 seconds), and the pre-pass tags it GPS_GAP_LONG_INSIDE_WINDOW and LOW_COVERAGE at weight 0.39. The trace shows two separate qualifying in-geofence runs, 60 seconds and 143 seconds, and it cannot show what happened between them. POL-NS-06(i) would let the runs be added (60 + 143 = 203 seconds), but that route requires a present and populated traffic advisory, and EV-ADVIS-02756-01 is MISSING at weight 0.00, so the runs cannot be summed. The driver's 'I waited the full time' statement carries no weight and fills nothing. Limb (c) is therefore undecided over the unobserved stretch, and an undecided limb supports neither the fee nor a refund of it.

The drivers' arguments. (1) Limbs (a) and (d) satisfied — accepted, but the fee needs all four limbs and limb (c) is undecided. (2) 'Dwell 400 seconds' — not accepted. The 400-second figure is the span that bridges the unobserved gap (60 + 197 + 143 = 400), not a measured continuous dwell; the trace cannot certify presence across the gap, and the derived block's own shortfall basis is the 143-second run. (3) Chat empty, no rider message — accepted; it defeats POL-NS-04 and POL-NS-03(i), but it decides fault allocation, not the dwell. (4) Fare ledger reconciles — accepted; no fare defect. (5) Anti-farming does not trip — accepted: no_show_terminations_30d is 0 and 0 / 85 completed trips is 0.0, so neither limb of the POL-NS-07 test holds, and I do not use prior_no_show_flags, which POL-NS-07 and POL-GEN-01 forbid for that test. (6) Compensation of $3.60 (80% of $4.50) — not reached: POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not, so no compensation issues. (7) No escalation route via the rider's or driver's dispute counters — accepted: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) do not fire; escalation arises under POL-NS-09(a) and (e) instead.

The rider's arguments. (1) 'Longest continuous run 143 seconds, 37 seconds short of 180, so refund in full' — the 143-second run is indeed the longest measured continuous dwell and it does fall short, but the 197 unobserved seconds could conceal continued presence, so limb (c) is undecided rather than failed and cannot carry a refund. (2) The $4.50 is charged and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00 — accepted as the state of the money; the fee is held rather than refunded. (3) POL-NS-06 is strict liability and the empty chat is irrelevant — accepted that the empty chat does not decide the dwell, but the clause still needs a measured dwell shorter than the minimum, and no such measurement can be certified here.

Why this escalates, and what the reviewer must settle. The deciding fact — whether the driver's in-geofence dwell reached 180 seconds — rests on a single artifact, EV-GPS-02756, at weight 0.39, which is below the platform confidence floor of 0.70 carried in this policy file (POL-GEN-02(2), POL-NS-09(a)); and that same artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(b) as the sole evidence for the deciding fact (POL-NS-09(e)). Escalation is terminal: no money moves and the $4.50 stays frozen. Open question for the reviewer: on the raw or full-resolution trace, did the driver remain inside the 50 m pickup radius continuously from 11:32:47 to 11:39:28, or did he leave and re-enter during 11:33:47–11:37:04? If he held position throughout, the fee stands at $4.50 and the driver's payout is $3.60; if the continuous dwell was under 180 seconds, POL-NS-06 refunds the $4.50 in full. If the reviewer needs more, the missing item is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02756-01. For routing: any monetary figure here ($4.50) would sit below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, but nothing executes while the fee is held.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

The driver's statement that traffic was heavy is an asserted external traffic cause, tested under POL-RD-13 against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. The only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-02803-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; no advisory covers this corridor and window, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the excuse carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run on the METERED fare model with the surge multiplier of 1.5 read from the fare breakdown EV-FARE-02803 (surge_multiplier field): recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.2 + 0.28 x 15.1) x 1.5) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.00 on-optimal-route ERP = 27.4420. There is no billing-integrity defect: the gantry is matched by a trace fix 7.52 m away, and the off-route ERP total is 0.00.

On POL-RD-06: the excess of 38.57% does not cross the 50% materiality line and 4.32 km does not cross the 8.0 km line, so this is not a MATERIAL deviation and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows. The platform's own derived deviation block independently records the status as 'no deviation'. Because neither establishment test passes, POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised, so your charge stands.

To the driver: no finding is made against you, and nothing is deducted. The 0.71 km variance sits inside the ordinary lane-change, U-turn and gantry-avoidance band the clause is designed to absorb.

On the money. That route is closed at its first condition, not at its arithmetic: POL-RD-02 applies only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, and it is not. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02805, weight 1.0) carries no ERP or toll lines (both totals 0.00) and no airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity has nothing to correct; the ledger reconciles to total_charged 18.54.

On the parties' claims. The driver's account in the counterparty statement ('I followed the navigation') cites no artifact, and POL-RD-08 gives an assertion that cites no evidence ID no weight; no clause makes the driver's account the test for the POL-RD-01 threshold, so it decides nothing here. A broader traffic excuse was asserted only in a claim the referee discarded for non-disclosure of the missing advisory's impairment, so it is not before me as a ground; separately, EV-ADVIS-02805-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no advisory covering this trip exists and POL-RD-03 could not have exonerated anything. On the profiles: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 172 completed trips in 90 days, well under the POL-RD-06 thresholds of 3 flags or a 0.05 ratio, so no repeat-deviation uplift and no conduct referral arise; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and I do not use it. The rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0 and substantiated 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift is not engaged and no profile factor counts against the rider. The trade of claims that the GPS trace is clean and that no escalation trigger fires is accepted: 99 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage and no gaps over 90 seconds, no jumps over 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 seconds, so the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; timestamps agree; and the refund is nil, far under the SGD 150.00 ceiling.

Confidence rests on EV-GPS-02805 and EV-TRIP-02805, each at weight_multiplier 1.0. Either party may appeal this provisional ruling once under POL-GEN-04 within 30 days.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the charge of S$21.10 stands and the disputed S$2.00 is not refunded.

Distance test (POL-RD-01). The platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-02806) measures the trip at 14.84 km; the booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-02806) is 14.0 km. I have used the trace figure of 14.84 km, as POL-RD-01 requires, and not the rounded 14.8 km convenience copy on the trip record. The excess is 0.84 km, which is 6.00% of the optimal distance. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only when the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and both tests must pass. The 0.84 km does clear the 0.8 km absolute gate by 0.04 km, but 6.00% is far below the 20% gate, so the establishment test fails and no route deviation exists on this trip. Both advocates reached this same conclusion and I accept it.

Trace integrity (POL-RD-07). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 117 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gap longer than 90 seconds and a maximum gap of 0.0 s. It is also COMPLETE at weight 1.0 in the pre-pass. The trace therefore governs the threshold test at full weight, and no impairment escalation arises.

Traffic excuse and the missing advisory (POL-RD-13). The driver's statement that he followed the navigation was not tested against a traffic advisory, because the only advisory in the bundle (EV-ADVIS-02806-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0 with no payload. POL-RD-13 provides that a traffic cause asserted for a measured deviation cannot be run without an advisory on file, and any such assertion carries no weight; but no deviation was measured here, so this changes nothing. The two discarded claims that cited the missing advisory are recorded in the audit below and were discarded by the referee for not naming its issue code.

Billing integrity (POL-RD-09). The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02806) reconciles to a charged total of 21.10, with zero ERP gantries, zero tolls, zero airport surcharge and a surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown. No phantom line or wrongly applied surcharge appears, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to correct and no billing-integrity referral is produced.

Profiles (POL-GEN-01). Both profiles are context only and none of their citable counters helps either side: the rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration test is not triggered; the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 of 230 completed trips, so the POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation pattern (and its conduct referral) is not available. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names and was correctly not substituted.

Outcome. With no deviation established, the rider's claim that the fare was higher than normal is not made out on the money side either: the optimal-route recomputation would be 20.3920 against 21.10, but POL-RD-02 never runs because POL-RD-01 fails. Under POL-GEN-03 the result is NO_ACTION: fare_breakdown.payment_status stays CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd stays 0.0. There is no monetary effect, so no execution-threshold question arises. The rider may appeal this provisional ruling once under POL-GEN-04.
